consensus_summary: Grass primarily symbolizes the transience, frailty, and mortality of human life/flesh ("all flesh is grass"), contrasting with God's enduring word; secondary uses include divine provision, short-lived wicked prosperity, and occasional abundance.
book_summary: Grass is the individual mortal—a man, flesh; and the field God farms unto harvest.
consensus_core_identification: frail/transient human flesh or people ("all flesh is grass")
book_core_identification: the individual mortal (a man, flesh) and the field God farms unto harvest
boundary_disagreement: Book includes the field (world farmed unto harvest) within grass's symbolic scope via Matt 13:38; consensus keeps grass as human frailty (or provision/prosperity) and treats the field as a distinct referent (the world/setting), not as grass itself.
material_contradiction: None; book retains the consensus flesh/mortal identification while adding a further referent.
rationale: Minimum cores share the Isa 40 identification of grass with individual mortal flesh/people. Book preserves that central referent but materially broadens by adding "the field God farms unto harvest" as co-identification, changing the extension/boundary without replacing the core. This is refinement (added cases), not equivalence, contradiction, or pure novelty.
strongest_objection: Matt 13:38 explicitly equates the field (not grass) with the world; applying it to make grass itself "the field" lacks direct warrant and may conflate distinct referents.
